subject: Request: Temporary throughput safety-net during Elm Street onboarding
messages:
From: Sara Mills <sara.mills@elmstreethealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: onboarding@elmstreethealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary throughput safety-net for onboarding window

Marcus —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We're planning to cut over three production services to Redwood inference next Wednesday (6/16) and the traffic forecast attached shows an expected 6-hour surge as 4 downstream services backfill caches. Our contract SLOs are comfortable for steady-state, but we're concerned Redwood's fairness-driven throttles and the standard rate cap will create a user-facing latency spike during the peak migration window.

Can we request a short, temporary throughput safety-net (48 hours) that would:
- Provision a transient priority token pool for Elm Street (isolate from fair-share pool)
- Temporarily raise per-route token rate by ~3x for the 6-hour window on 6/16 02:00–08:00 UTC
- Add a short rollback and monitoring policy so we don't affect other customers longer than necessary

I've attached our traffic forecast and a one-page migration runbook. If you need a legal form or PO, let me know — we can sign whatever's required quickly.

Appreciate a quick confirmation since we need to finalize the cutover plan by EOD tomorrow.

— Sara
Sara Mills
Head of Platform Ops, Elm Street Health
Sara.mills@elmstreethealth.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: migration_traffic_forecast_q2.csv (csv), migration_runbook.pdf (pdf)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mills <sara.mills@elmstreethealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary throughput safety-net for onboarding window

Sara — thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments, they look useful. Short answer: we can usually support transient priority capacity for migrations, but there are a few guardrails we need to run through (SLA amendment, monitoring hooks, and a safety rollback).

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal technical triage (I'll loop in Karthik to confirm feasibility and the expected latency profile under a 3x short window).
2) We prepare a temporary SLO amendment doc and an exception form (legal + procurement sign-off).
3) If approved, we create a 48-hour priority token pool scoped to your account and attach telemetry dashboards for token usage and tail latency.

Karthik — can you confirm the operations side (whether we can create a short-lived token pool that bypasses fair-share for the specified routes and what the rollback looks like)? Also, please note the proposed window: 2027-06-16 02:00–08:00 UTC.

Sara — I'll aim to get a formal reply within 3 hours so you can proceed.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0123

Attachment: sla-exception-form.pdf (draft)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sara Mills <sara.mills@elmstreethealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary throughput safety-net for onboarding window

On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 10:05 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Karthik — can you confirm the operations side (whether we can create a short-lived token pool that bypasses fair-share for the specified routes and what the rollback looks like)?

We can. Quick technical notes:
- We will create an "onboarding_pool" (48h TTL) attached to Elm Street's account, scoped to the three production routes you called out. That pool will have its own token bucket and will be policed before fair-share to ensure isolation.
- We can increase per-route rate limit for the window by a multiplier (3x as requested); this is enforced at the routing layer.
- Rollback plan: automated revert at window end + an immediate manual kill switch in Console (we'll send a PagerDuty page to Redwood infra ops if we detect >5% error rate increase or tail latency >350ms for 5m).
- Observability: we will provision a dashboard with token consumption, median/tail latency, and queue depth. We'll stream metrics to your SRE Slack channel and to our internal incident channel.

Two caveats:
1) We need a short amendment to the SLA to cover the temporary priority pool semantics and liability during the exception window.
2) If another customer is already using a global emergency priority for the same hardware zone, we may need to shift your traffic regionally (we'll confirm).

Assuming Marcus/legal sign-off, my engineering team can stand up the pool and dashboards within 4 hours of approval.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Mills <sara.mills@elmstreethealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary throughput safety-net for onboarding window

Circling on the contract/procurement side: legal is okay to sign an SLA amendment for a 48-hour exception so long as Elm Street signs the standard exception form and confirms payment terms (we can accept a signed form + post-cutover invoice). I've attached the exception form draft (also linked in the thread).

Two administrative notes:
- Please confirm the exact route names and any webhook endpoints that should be excluded from the increased rate (we typically exclude bulk admin endpoints).
- We'll add a one-time professional services tag to the invoice for the priority pool provisioning (small flat fee).

If Sara can return the signed form by EOD today, legal and infra will prepare the pool and dashboards for the 6/16 window.

Best,
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachment: sla-exception-form.pdf (updated)
From: Sara Mills <sara.mills@elmstreethealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary throughput safety-net for onboarding window

Thanks, all — this is great.

We signed the attached exception form and added the route list (prod-api/v1/infer, prod-stream/v1/respond, prod-batch/v1/embeds). We can exclude the admin bulk endpoints as suggested. We've also uploaded a signed PO to your procurement portal (HubSpot link below).

Please proceed with:
- Create the onboarding_pool (48h TTL) scoped to the three routes and set rate multiplier to 3x for 2027-06-16 02:00–08:00 UTC
- Send the Console link to the dashboard and the kill-switch instructions
- Confirm invoicing details for the one-time provisioning fee

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll monitor closely and will notify you immediately if we see anything abnormal.

— Sara
Sara Mills
Head of Platform Ops, Elm Street Health
